messages:
Maya Chen: hey all — i'm Maya, joined eng-platform today. trying to get kubectl talking to our cluster. downloaded the kubeconfig from the onboarding portal and merged into ~/.kube/config but kubectl just errors: "The connection to the server localhost:8080 was refused". can someone help grant me access to a dev namespace + check my context? thanks!
Samir Patel: welcome @Maya Chen :tada: quick q — did you merge the kubeconfig or are you using the one from the portal as a separate file?
Maya Chen: i merged. ran: `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/redwood-kubeconfig kubectl config view --merge > /tmp/merged && mv /tmp/merged ~/.kube/config`
Samir Patel: ok nice. try `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev` then `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev`
Maya Chen: ran that — `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev` worked but `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev` returns "no"
Javier Gomez: hey @Maya Chen — looks like you don't have a RoleBinding in the dev namespace yet. @infra-netops / iam team: can we create a RoleBinding dev-onboard-maya that binds the clusterrole `edit` to user `maya.chen@redwood.ai` in namespace `dev-maya` (or let @Maya have a personal onboarding ns)?
iam-bot: Request received: iam.create_rolebinding ticket #INC-5421. Assigned to infra-team. ETA ~1h.
Javier Gomez: also check that the user field in your kubeconfig matches the OIDC identity (no extra suffix). run: `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.users[0].user.auth-provider.config.id-token}'` to verify there's a token present
Maya Chen: token present. also would prefer a personal ns so i can port-forward test pods without touching dev. can we get dev-maya?
Samir Patel: we usually create dev-<initials> for new hires. @Javier can you make `dev-maya` or `dev-mc`? otherwise if RBAC allows Maya can do `kubectl create ns dev-maya`
Javier Gomez: created namespace `dev-maya` and applied RoleBinding (bound `edit` to maya.chen@redwood.ai). try `kubectl auth can-i create pods -n dev-maya`
Maya Chen: `kubectl auth can-i create pods -n dev-maya` -> yes!! thanks. trying port-forward now: `kubectl port-forward svc/local-redis 6379:6379 -n dev-maya` — it prints `Forwarding from 127.0.0.1:6379 -> 6379` but my app can't connect; it seems stuck/hangs
Samir Patel: are you on corp VPN or behind a bastion? If the cluster is private we sometimes need to tunnel via the bastion. gcloud ssh to `redwood-bastion` with an -L flag is one option.
Maya Chen: i'm on VPN. tried `gcloud compute ssh redwood-bastion -- -L 6379:localhost:6379` but got `ssh: connect to host 34.12.1.1 port 22: Connection timed out` — maybe bastion IP changed after maintenance
Javier Gomez: infra had a small network change this morning. @infra-netops can you confirm NAT and bastion reachability? In the meantime, you can use `kubectl proxy` as a workaround to reach service endpoints from localhost. eg: 
```
kubectl proxy --port=8001 --accept-hosts='^.*$'
# then from local machine
curl http://localhost:8001/api/v1/namespaces/dev-maya/services/local-redis:6379/proxy/
```
Maya Chen: tried the proxy approach and was able to curl the service metrics. port-forward still flakes but i can continue dev work. really appreciate the quick help everyone!
iam-bot: INC-5421 updated: RoleBinding applied to namespace dev-maya for maya.chen@redwood.ai by Javier Gomez. Ticket closed.
Samir Patel: welcome again @Maya — if you want a quick tour of common debug commands, ping me and i'll drop a small runbook in this channel. :coffee:
